html:
The Wilyakali are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country around the Darling River basin in far west New South Wales and across the border into South Australia. Their lands centred on what are now the towns of Broken Hill and Silverton. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their country is dry ranges and saltbush plains, where people moved between rock holes and creeks. In 1883 a boundary rider found silver, lead and zinc at Broken Hill, and the mine there became one of the richest in the world and the start of the company BHP. The town grew fast on Wilyakali land. Neighbours on the map include the Danggali, the Malyangaba and the Barkindji. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
